name: Central Nervous System Cystic Malformation

criteria.description: Presence of cystic lesion within the central nervous system confirmed by MRI or CT imaging
Neurological symptoms attributable to cystic malformation such as focal neurological deficits or increased intracranial pressure
Exclusion of infectious, neoplastic, or vascular causes for cystic CNS lesions
Histopathological confirmation when biopsy or surgical resection is performed

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging evidence of CNS cystic lesion plus clinical symptoms consistent with cystic malformation and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological supported by clinical presentation; histopathology is confirmatory if available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intracranial cystic lesion visible on neuroimaging
searchTerms: brain cyst visible on MRI or CT
gradual worsening of localized neurological problems
progressive weakness or numbness in one area

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting caused by increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment or developmental delay in pediatric cases

searchTerms: loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal unless secondary infection or hemorrhage present
imaging: MRI showing well-demarcated cystic lesions within CNS parenchyma or ventricles
CT scan showing hypodense cystic areas
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; may be sporadic or associated with developmental anomalies
other: Histopathology reveals cyst wall lined by glial or ependymal cells depending on cyst type

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
New onset seizures or focal deficits
